page.title: Kubernetes
page.description: Connect a Kubernetes cluster with one DaemonSet; its GPU nodes become nodes here.
page.empty: No Kubernetes cluster yet. Connect one and its GPU nodes show up in the node list.

clusterUid.notEnrolledHint: No node has joined from this cluster yet.

actions.revokeHelp: Nodes already connected keep working. New nodes can no longer join with this command.
actions.deleteHelp: Only the cluster record here is removed. Delete the DaemonSet in Kubernetes yourself. A cluster that still has nodes cannot be deleted.

manifest.failed: The manifest could not be loaded

drawer.title: Connect a Kubernetes cluster
drawer.name: Name
drawer.nameRequired: Enter a name for the cluster
drawer.serverUrlHelp: The address the agents in the cluster reach this server at. It must be reachable from the cluster's Pods.
drawer.serverUrlInvalid: Enter an http:// or https:// address
drawer.vendorHelp: The vendor of the cards on the cluster's GPU nodes. A cluster has one.
drawer.poolsHelp: The entry runs on the nodes of the pools ticked here, which must all be of one vendor; the entry takes their vendor.
drawer.nodeSelectorHelp: Optional. Comma-separated key=value pairs; only Kubernetes nodes with all of these labels join. Empty means every node.
drawer.namespaceHelp: Where the DaemonSet and its resources are created.
drawer.stateDirHelp: The agent's directory on the host. Set a different one to let the agent run beside an agent already installed on the host; empty uses the default shown in the box.
drawer.agentImageSourceHelp: Nodes pull the published agent image from here. Clusters in mainland China usually cannot reach Docker Hub: choose Huawei Cloud SWR. A cluster of a cloud account starts with the registry its region reaches.
drawer.defaultsFailed: The defaults could not be loaded
drawer.defaultsFailedHelp: Fields left empty still take the server's defaults; the hints and the vendor list are missing.
drawer.agentImageHelp: Runs your own image instead (for example a copy in a private registry) rather than pulling from the registry above.
drawer.imagePullSecretHelp: For an agent image in a registry that needs a login: the name of a docker-registry Secret in the namespace, created before applying.
drawer.runtimeClassHelp: NVIDIA only: the RuntimeClass instance Pods reach the GPUs with. Empty decides on each node: the cluster's nvidia RuntimeClass when it has one (k3s), the node's default runtime otherwise (as on managed Kubernetes).
drawer.containerdSocketHelp: Path on the node. Empty lets the agents find it themselves; set it only for an unusual location.
drawer.apiServerHelp: Only for nodes where nothing serves Service addresses (no kube-proxy or replacement, such as KubeEdge or OpenYurt edge nodes). The address must be in the API server's certificate. Empty uses the cluster's kubernetes Service.
drawer.enginePortsHelp: Host ports the inference engines listen on. It must not overlap the cluster's NodePort range (30000-32767 by default).
drawer.priorityHelp: The PriorityClass value of gpuworks hold and instance pods; larger runs first, and ordinary pods are 0. When a node runs short of memory or disk, Kubernetes evicts lower-priority pods first.
drawer.allowPreemptionHelp: Off (the default), a card gpuworks cannot fit waits, and the scheduler never evicts your other pods for it. On, with HAMi or ACK GPU sharing the scheduler may evict lower-priority pods for a hold pod.
drawer.idleReturnSeconds: Seconds idle before a card is returned
drawer.idleReturnHelp: A card borrowed from Kubernetes goes back to it after sitting idle for this long.
drawer.keepCardsHelp: Never hand borrowed cards back to Kubernetes.
drawer.fromSource: From {{source}}: the node selector is set for the chosen node pool.

created.title: Cluster {{name}} is ready
created.note: Run this command in the cluster. The GPU nodes it selects show up in the node list by themselves.
created.secret: The command contains the connect token. Treat it like a password.
created.noteSource: Next, apply the manifest to the cluster, one way or the other:
created.byGpuworksHelp: gpuworks uses short-lived cluster credentials issued to the cloud account now (valid 15 minutes, discarded after use, never stored), checks first, and lists the objects for you to confirm before applying.
created.byKubectl: Or run this in the cluster yourself
created.applyBlocked: gpuworks cannot apply it for you

blocked.no_source: This cluster was added by hand, so gpuworks has no way into it. Run the kubectl command in the cluster.
blocked.private_api: The cloud reports this cluster's API server has no public address, so gpuworks cannot reach it. Run the kubectl command from inside the cluster's network.
blocked.revoked: The connect token is revoked, so the manifest cannot be applied again. Removing it from the cluster still works.

stalled.title: No node has joined yet
stalled.intro: The cluster has waited a while for its first node and none has joined. Look at the agent DaemonSet and its Pods in the cluster:
stalled.pull: Pods in ImagePullBackOff: the agent image cannot be pulled. For a registry that needs a login, create a docker-registry Secret in the namespace and name it as the image pull secret when creating the cluster.
stalled.runtimeClass: A DaemonSet event says the RuntimeClass does not exist: the cluster has no such RuntimeClass; leave it empty and the agent decides.
stalled.selector: The DaemonSet wants 0 Pods: the node selector selects no node.
stalled.connect: Pods run but no node appears: the agents cannot reach the server address; read the agent log.

pools.title: Node pools of {{name}}
pools.intro: The entry runs on the nodes of the ticked GPU node pools of its cloud cluster. Saving changes gpuworks's record; the cluster follows when the manifest is applied again.
pools.legacy: This entry selects nodes by a node selector
pools.legacyHelp: It was made before node pools were chosen: it selects nodes with "{{selector}}". Saving node pools replaces that selector, and the entry then runs on those pools alone.
pools.loadFailed: Cannot read the cluster's node pools
pools.clusterGone: The cloud account no longer lists this cluster.
pools.none: The cluster has no GPU node pool to choose from.
pools.savedHelp: Apply the manifest again so the cluster follows (or run kubectl apply again). Agents on node pools taken away exit; their nodes stay in the node list until they are cleaned up as offline.

operation.applyIntro: gpuworks will create or update the objects below in cluster {{cluster}}, with short-lived credentials the cloud account {{account}} issues now (not stored).
operation.removeIntro: gpuworks will delete the objects below from cluster {{cluster}}, with short-lived credentials the cloud account {{account}} issues now (not stored): the agents, hold pods and instance pods go with the DaemonSet, and the cards go back to Kubernetes.
operation.checking: Asking the cluster to check these changes (dry run; nothing changes)…
operation.checkedApply: Checked. Nothing is applied until you confirm.
operation.checkedRemove: Checked. Nothing is deleted until you confirm.
operation.appliedNext: The selected GPU nodes appear on the Nodes page in about half a minute.

failed.kubeconfig: The cloud account did not issue usable cluster credentials
